title: MONSTER ATM and Food Dispenser
tagline: Build an automated banking and snack dispenser with PIN authentication and servo dispensing!

phases.instructions: Gather the 4x4 membrane keypad, 1602 I2C LCD, SG90 micro-servo motor, and cardboard chute or cup.
verificationCheckpoints: SG90 micro servo with arm attached

phases.instructions: Connect LCD to A4/A5 I2C lines. Connect keypad rows to pins 9-6 and columns to pins 5-2. Connect Servo PWM signal to Pin 10.
Ensure the servo dispenser door flap can rotate freely 90 degrees without binding against the dispenser wall.
verificationCheckpoints: Flap moves smoothly through 90 degree arc
Verify power lines have solid breadboard connections

phases.instructions: Review how the Arduino manages banking states: AWAIT_PIN -> VALIDATING -> DISPENSING -> LOCKED.
phases.codeExplanation:
- State machine prompts user for 4-digit PIN on the LCD.
- Keys typed are accumulated into inputPin string.
- When inputPin == MASTER_PIN, dispenseReward() triggers servo to swing 90 degrees for 2 seconds.
- After dispensing, door closes and system re-locks automatically.
verificationCheckpoints: Understand string accumulation for keypad digits
Understand timed servo actuation for mechanical dispensing

phases.instructions: Upload sketch, load a candy or bead into the chute, type PIN '7788' and press '#' to watch your ATM dispense!
verificationCheckpoints: Key presses appear as asterisks on LCD
Correct PIN opens servo chute and drops treat

phases.instructions: Bravo! You integrated user interaction, display feedback, and mechanical actuation into a complete product.

story: Build an automated Monster ATM and snack treat dispenser! Your monster customers enter their secret 4-digit PIN on the matrix keypad; if approved, the LCD welcomes them and a servo arm sweeps open the vault chute to dispense a treat.

troubleshooting.symptom: Servo twitches and resets Arduino when activating
troubleshooting.cause: Servo inrush current causes 5V rail voltage drop (brownout)
troubleshooting.solution: Add a 100uF electrolytic capacitor across 5V and GND near the servo power pins.
diagnosticSteps: Servo draws high inrush current causing brownout reset.
Add external 4xAA battery pack with shared ground to Arduino GND.
